text:
marta: quick follow-up from the ingest architecture sync — we've got two competing proposals for carrying cost/identity through the edge: header contraction (compact headers on every request) vs enveloping (wrap payloads with an attrib envelope). want to surface tradeoffs and pick an experiment.

leo: short list i see — headers = small perf win, simpler for proxies, but brittle for long-lived connections (stale tokens) and hard for binary protocols. enveloping = explicit, easier to evolve, but adds bytes and requires downstream fanout changes. :thinking_face:

sam: +1. also headers leak into logs more easily which is good for debuggability but bad for PII. we need a canonical redaction/allowlist if we go header-first.

zane: real worry with headers is fragmentation across SDKs. mobile SDKs might omit header if connection pooled or if custom transport. envelope guarantees the attribute travels with the payload.

marta: agreed. for cost attribution specifically we need the billing_key present at the earliest router so we can tag traces and meter. how tolerant are we of late enrichment? does anyone have numbers for % of requests we currently enrich late? ingest-bot: telemetry snapshot: sample-rate=0.01 -> late_enrich_ratio=0.083 (past 7d)

leo: ok interesting. 8.3% late enrich at sampled rate maps to ~similar order overall. that's nontrivial if billing attribution must be perfect for chargeback.

sam: proposal: 3-stage approach: (1) header-contraction opt-in for high-throughput paths with SDKs updated to include canonical header; (2) envelope as fallback for clients we don't control; (3) server-side reconciliation job to backfill traces missing billing_key using the envelope/train of events.

zane: sounds pragmatic. couple of nitty gritty: header shape, TTL semantics, what to do on reconnects. suggest header key name `X-RW-Obs` with semicolon-separated kv: `X-RW-Obs: tenant=acme;billing=pk_123;ttl=168h`

marta: sample header example looks good. we should *not* put PII in there — only opaque ids. also TTL is important so we reject stale billing.

sam: envelope example (for reference):
```
{
  "envelope": {
    "attrs": {"tenant":"acme","billing":"pk_123","ttl":"168h"},
    "payload": <original bytes>
  }
}
```
leakiness + perf: envelope adds ~80-140 bytes depending on serialization. headers add ~40-60 bytes on average.

leo: operational impacts: proxies need to index headers for routing and sampling decisions. envelope requires us to change fanout and some of our async queues to unpack. that's more invasive.

marta: concrete next steps: 1) implement header-contraction shim in proxy + SDK bump (sam to own), 2) add envelope acceptor on ingest path (zane to spike minimal unpack), 3) telemetry: add metrics for `ingest.attr.presence` and `ingest.attr.source` (header|envelope|late_backfill) (leo to own).

sam: I'll open the PR for the SDK change and a short RFC snippet for header key format.

zane: will prototype minimal envelope acceptor this week and report perf numbers.

marta: thanks — let's reconvene Fri 10am, sync notes in the RFC thread. if we see >1% failure on header propagation during canary, rollback to envelope-only for that client. :thumbsup:

ingest-bot: scheduled reminder: reconvene meeting set for Fri 10:00 UTC (auto-reminder 30m before).
